name: Starter: Czech
about: Czech word order and cases in real, everyday sentences.

words.mít se: to be doing, to fare (jak se máš: how are you)
words.jít: to go, usually on foot; to go or attend somewhere (pojď: come)
words.líbit se: to please (líbí se mi: I like it)
words.rád: glad; likes to, gladly (masculine; feminine ráda; rád vařím: I like cooking)
words.chléb: bread (here accusative chleba; chléb is also possible)
words.jet: to go (by car, bus or train)
words.zima: cold; winter (je mi zima: I'm cold)
words.hezky: nicely (bude hezky: it'll be nice out)

jak-se-máš.about: Literally, how do you have yourself? Answer with Dobře, díky (fine, thanks).

jak-se-jmenuješ.about: Literally, how do you call yourself? Answer with Jmenuju se and your name.

promiňte.about: To get someone's attention or say sorry: polite to one person, or to more than one; one friend gets Promiň.

dal-bych-si.about: Literally, I'd give myself; a woman says dala bych si.

platit-prosím.about: Literally, to pay, please: how you ask for the check.

dej-mi-vědět.about: A fixed request: tell me, keep me posted.

concept.line: The verb's ending marks person and number, though some forms are the same: (já) bydlím, (ty) bydlíš, (on, ona) bydlí, (my) bydlíme, (oni) bydlí.

words.means: reflexive pronoun/particle; often has no separate English translation

concept.line: A Czech verb often marks person and number, so já (I), ty (you) and my (we) are usually left out when it's clear who: Bydlím v Praze (I live in Prague).

words.means: jsem = I am; jsi = you are; nejsem = I am not

concept.line: Czech nouns are masculine, feminine or neuter.

words.means: mám = I have; máš = you have; nemám = I don't have

concept.line: A yes/no question often keeps the order of a statement and is signaled by question intonation; a question word like kde, co or jak usually comes first, and Czech adds no do.

words.means: mluvíš = you speak; mluvím = I speak
nerozumím = I don't understand; rozumíš = you understand

concept.line: The accusative marks many direct objects: káva becomes Piju kávu, and masculine nouns for people and animals change too.

words.means: bydlíš = you live; bydlím = I live; bydlí = lives
jdu = I go; jdeš = you are going; jde = goes

concept.line: Czech has no words for a, an or the; context and word order do their work: Jsem učitel; Na stole leží kniha.

words.means: already; now (as in 'I have to go now')
pracuji = I work; pracovat = to work
